title: Wednesday Teacher Plan
note: 30-minute day. Blooket opener. One turn-in per class: the exit ticket.

4th Period.topic: Strategy pattern, Day 3: trace the swap
4th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can trace how a brick uses its strategy each frame, and say what changes when I swap slide for stayStill.
4th Period.exitTicket: What changes when you swap a brick from slide to stayStill, and what stays the same?
prep: Day 3 handout attached to Strategy Pattern; exit ticket posted
Trace table drawn on the board: Frame | Brick A (slide) | Brick B (stayStill)

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Tuesday: slide changes x, startX, turning around, speed.
tips: Load the Blooket_*_Wed_Nov4 set before the bell.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Quick review of the most-missed questions, then read the goal: By the end of class, I can trace how a brick uses its strategy each frame, and say what changes when I swap slide for stayStill.

segments.title: We do: trace 2 bricks
segments.do: Fill in the table with the class: A (slide, speed 2) goes 102, 104, 106; B (stayStill) stays 100. Then swap A to stayStill and trace 3 more frames: A stays at 106.
tips: Answer key: A 102/104/106, B 100/100/100. After the swap, A's x stops changing; the loop is unchanged.

segments.title: Partner check: point to the swap
segments.do: Partners point to the one word in the brick factory (slide or stayStill) and to brick.move(brick) in the loop.
segments.why: Checks for understanding before the exit ticket.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: On Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Full answer: the brick stops moving (x stays the same); the loop in update() stays the same; only move: changes in the brick factory.

watchFor: Students thinking update() must change to swap.

6th Period.topic: Warren Truss Build, Day 3: join + deck (one strike)
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, my group's two side trusses are joined ¼ stick apart, and our bridge has a cardboard deck glued on at every bottom joint.
6th Period.exitTicket: Where did your group glue the deck, and why there?
prep: Day 3 handout attached to the exit ticket
Both side trusses and Joints That Hold cards out
Cardboard, paper, glue sticks, scissors. No tape.
Make one folded deck yourself to show

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Tuesday: matching sides, stack check, glue on faces, fold-over tabs, paper wraps, the 4 glue steps.
tips: Load the Blooket_*_Wed_Nov4 set before the bell.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Quick review of the most-missed questions, then read the goal: By the end of class, my group's two side trusses are joined ¼ stick apart, and our bridge has a cardboard deck glued on at every bottom joint.

segments.title: You do: join + deck
segments.do: Roles by birthday (Joiner, Deck Builder, Materials Manager, Checker). Join with tabbed cross pieces if not done. Deck = one rectangle, 1 1/2 sticks long, 1/4 stick + 2 glue squares wide, both long edges scored and folded down, tabs glued on the outside at every bottom joint.
segments.why: Apply; the folded tabs turn the 90-degree joint into a face joint.
tips: Call a strike at once, calmly.
Groups still on side 2: finish it; deck tomorrow.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: On Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Full answer: at the bottom joints / on the outside faces of the bottom chords, because that's where the triangles meet, and tabs give the glue a face to hold.

segments.title: Clean up + set to dry
segments.do: Bridge flat on the shelf, scissors counted.

watchFor: Deck laid edge-on with no tabs.

7th Period.goal: By the end of class, my group predicted, then tested our bridge with water bottles and marked exactly where it failed first.
7th Period.exitTicket: Where did your bridge fail first, and why do you think it failed there?
prep: Day 3 handout attached to Bridge Deck and Load Test
About 5 full 16.9 oz water bottles per group
Bridges handed back; one test station per group (2 desks a 1-stick gap apart)
Backpacks or jackets for under the gap

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Tuesday: why 90-degree glue failed, faces vs. edges, paper wraps, roof, X-brace.
tips: Load the Blooket_*_Wed_Nov4 set before the bell.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Quick review of the most-missed questions, then read the goal: By the end of class, my group predicted, then tested our bridge with water bottles and marked exactly where it failed first.

segments.title: Roles
segments.do: Youngest Loader, 2nd youngest Spotter, 2nd oldest Recorder, oldest Checker. Group of 3: Checker also Spotter. Group of 5: two Spotters.
segments.why: Complex Instruction: the Checker owns STOP.

segments.title: Set up + predict
segments.do: Bridge across the 1-stick gap, resting 1/4 stick on each desk; soft surface under; cardboard platform (1/2 x 1/2 stick) on the middle top joint. Recorder writes the prediction (bottles + where it will fail) on the name label.
segments.why: Predict before testing (rigor for this class).
tips: Loading on top because the roof blocks the deck. A deck-only group can lay bottles on the deck instead; note that in the turn-in.

segments.title: Test 1
segments.do: One bottle on its side at a time, wait 5 s, Checker says go. STOP at the first crack, lean, sag or popped joint; bottles off right away. Recorder writes Test 1: N bottles (held before failure) and marks an X at the failure.
segments.why: Analyze: find the weak spot to fix tomorrow.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: On Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Full answer: names a spot (a joint, the deck, a diagonal, the roof) plus a reason (glue let go, edge joint, strip bent in the middle, no bracing).

watchFor: Groups not stopping at the first crack.
The Test 1 number must be on the label for Friday.

accommodations: Goal reviewed after the Blooket; numbered steps; worked examples (trace table, folded deck, test diagram); two sentence frames.
Pictures for key words (swap, trace; deck, tab; platform, fail); partner talk before writing.
Lexend Deca; steps read aloud; speech-to-text OK.
Short 30-minute chunks with a visual timer; hands-on roles (Loader, Spotter, Joiner).
Dictated exit tickets; floors: 8th traces brick A only; 7th glues the deck at 2 joints; 6th says where it failed.
frameworks: Products advance: a traced strategy, a decked bridge, a tested bridge.
Roles with authority: the Checker calls STOP and approves every piece.
Short day, small goals; failure in Test 1 is planned and safe.
